image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Triceratops skull fossil (or high-fidelity replica) mounted on a metal stand in an outdoor setting. The skull features the characteristic three horns (two large brow horns, one smaller nasal horn) and a massive, solid bony frill. The bone appears weathered, brown/grey, with visible cracks and texture. The background consists of green foliage, palm trees, and a distant hillside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns curving forward/upward and a smaller nasal horn. They are structurally sound and correctly positioned relative to the eye sockets.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows a bare fossilized skull. The 'beak' described in the taxonomy refers to the keratinous rhamphotheca which covers the premaxilla in life. In this fossil, only the bony core is visible, and the very tip of the snout appears slightly damaged or incomplete. Therefore, the 'sharp keratinous edge' is not present/testable as it is biological soft tissue not preserved here.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the skull only. The body and limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is the dominant feature of the image, extending significantly backward. Its width clearly exceeds the length of the facial portion of the skull, matching the morphological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated). The surface texture is consistent with fossilized bone (rough/weathered rather than 'smooth' like fresh bone, but structurally solid). Epoccipitals are visible along the margin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a bare skull; no skin, scales, or body coverings are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the frame.
The tail is not visible in the frame.
